summary: This function generates a git commit message by sending the staged code changes to a local AI model, then displays the result and asks the user to confirm, edit, or reject it before actually committing. The design ensures nothing gets committed without explicit user action — just pressing Enter does nothing.

explanations.6: This line registers the function in a lookup table so the help system knows about it and can display what it does.
explanations.7: This declares that the ai-commit command doesn't take any parameters from the user.
explanations.11: This calls a helper function to extract just the staged changes (the diff), and if that fails for any reason, the whole function exits early with an error.
explanations.13: This is a multi-line string variable that contains the exact instructions we'll send to the AI model; the ${diff} at the end will be replaced with the actual staged changes.
explanations.19: This sends the prompt to the local AI service and stores whatever message it generates, again exiting early if the AI service isn't available.
explanations.24: The -n flag prevents a newline from being printed after the prompt text, so the user's response appears on the same line.
explanations.26: The -k1 flags mean 'read exactly one character without waiting for Enter', so the user just presses a single key and we respond immediately.
explanations.30: If the user pressed 'y' or 'Y', this commits using the AI-generated message as-is.
explanations.31: If the user pressed 'e' or 'E', the -e flag opens their text editor to let them modify the message before committing.
